newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia plans new aviation rules to improve safety.
newsitem.headline: Russia plans new aviation rules to improve safety.

text.p: Russia's aviation authorities said on Wednesday they planned to introduce new federal aviation rules by the end of this year aimed at improving air safety standards.

Yuri Karetsky, head of the pilots' department of the Federal Aviation Service, said the rules would reduce the number of safety-related incidents involving Russian carriers formed after the break up of Soviet airline monopoly Aeroflot in 1992.
"We want to move closer to the international air regulation system," Karetsky told Reuters.
Karetsky said the rules -- which he said were still being finalised -- would be presented soon for consideration by experts of the International Air Transport Association (IATA).
"Later they will be approved by the Russian government," he said.

Karetsky said 390 airlines were currently registered in Russia. Many of them are struggling financially and aviation experts say tighter enforcement of safety rules would force riskier carriers out of business.
"We hope that the number of carriers will be reduced by 150 over the next two years because many are in a bad financial position," Karetsky said.
IATA's director of security services held talks on air security with Aeroflot officials in March. He said the flagship Russian carrier had achieved international standards.

Aeroflot said it had invested 12 billion roubles ($2.1 million) to improve its air security. But some smaller carriers lack the resources to improve standards and travellers say baggage inspection is occasionally lax at some airports.
Many Russian passengers try to travel with weapons, officials say. The Federal Aviation Service said about 44,000 arms were confiscated at airports last year, compared with 63,000 in 1995.
But there was only one hijack attempt last year, according to the head of Aeroflot's security service.
In that incident, a hijacker with a knife threatened passengers on a flight from Moscow to Nigeria before he was arrested on board by Aeroflot security staff.
